final_recommendation: The room converged on a dual-track rescue: a CHF 100bn SNB liquidity facility with broadened collateral, a UBS merger commitment by Monday close, and an Article 25 resolution clause with AT1 write-down as the binding backstop if UBS walks. All three components publish simultaneously Sunday 6 a.m., with execution mechanics validated by a Saturday night operational drill.
minority_objections: AT1 representative demanded explicit no-repricing guarantees on collateral valuation to prevent creditor litigation claims that the facility was false advertising
Wealth client insisted on simultaneous publication timing with zero gap between UBS commitment and Article 25 clause to prevent panic velocity in deposit outflows
UBS CEO required written cost cap on SNB facility exposure before signing, refusing to be a stalking horse for an open-ended government guarantee
key_conflicts: Federal Council vs FINMA on who authorizes loss-absorption language and AT1 write-down clauses before a buyer is confirmed
SNB vs Federal Council on whether deposit guarantee should be time-limited (Monday close) or open-ended, with SNB insisting on expiry to cap taxpayer exposure
UBS vs Federal Council on three merger conditions (deposit guarantee, 50bn loss buffer, regulatory indemnity) with UBS threatening to walk if not locked in writing by Sunday
AT1 holders vs FINMA on whether write-down language blocks judicial review and negotiation windows, with creditors threatening immediate litigation if ambiguous
Wealth clients vs CS CEO on whether relationship manager scripts would be softened for client comfort versus delivered verbatim to ensure consistency
key_concessions: Federal Council agreed to 50bn loss buffer as capped public loan against acquired assets, accepting defined taxpayer exposure to secure UBS participation
SNB agreed to time-limited deposit backstop through Monday close only, expiring into resolution if merger fails, capping open-ended guarantee risk
FINMA agreed to prospective-only regulatory indemnity (post-March 17) for UBS, excluding past three years of findings to limit legal exposure
UBS agreed to sign AT1 write-down clause accepting subordinated losses if merger proceeds, in exchange for the three locked government commitments
CS CEO agreed to conditional RM script based on Saturday drill results, softening exact timing language if execution showed any friction
red_lines: Federal Council: no open-ended loss-absorption commitment or AT1 write-down authority without confirmed buyer and defined rescue structure
UBS: will not sign merger without written commitments on deposit guarantee, 50bn loss buffer, and regulatory indemnity by Sunday close
SNB: will not deploy 100bn facility if capital backstop remains ambiguous or if collateral framework is still under negotiation Monday morning
AT1 holders: will litigate immediately if write-down clause contains any negotiation window or good-faith discussion language
FINMA: Monday close is hard trigger for Article 25 resolution with no discretion or Tuesday negotiation window if UBS walks
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Operational execution risk of the 08:30-to-09:00 settlement window was not validated until Round 8, leaving the entire liquidity protocol untested until Saturday night drill
Collateral re-marking costs and valuation methodology under Monday stress conditions remained unresolved through Round 10, creating ambiguity on whether 50bn cap covered re-pricing
Deposit outflow velocity assumptions (20-30bn in first two hours if announcement has gaps) were raised but never stress-tested against the 50bn facility cap
Litigation risk from AT1 holders was acknowledged but the actual enforceability of no-judicial-review language was never legally validated before publication
Relationship manager script consistency enforcement mechanism was questioned but never operationalized beyond spot-checking calls
downstream_risk_variables: Saturday 22:00 drill result determines whether Sunday RM script includes exact 08:30-to-09:00 timing or softens to 'mechanics confirmed live'
Simultaneous 6 a.m. Sunday publication timing of UBS commitment and Article 25 clause determines deposit outflow velocity Monday morning
Collateral valuation lock-in (no re-pricing rights under stress) determines whether AT1 holders can claim facility was false and demand negotiation
UBS board decision Sunday night after seeing drill results and written government commitments determines whether merger closes or resolution triggers Monday
Monday morning deposit velocity in first two hours determines whether 50bn facility cap is breached before 10:00, forcing mid-run resolution trigger
uncertainty_notes: The 50bn SNB cost cap remains ambiguous on whether it covers collateral re-marking costs or only liquidity draw. The Saturday drill has not yet validated clean 08:30-to-09:00 execution. The enforceability of the no-judicial-review clause in the AT1 write-down language has not been legally tested. Deposit outflow velocity assumptions (20-30bn/hour if announcement has gaps) have not been stress-tested against facility capacity. The operational mechanism for enforcing RM script consistency across all teams remains unspecified beyond spot-checking.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: SNB in R1: 'we can push liquidity out the door today, but if you're not ready to stand behind write-downs or a guarantee on the capital side, Credit Suisse's creditors know it' — drove the dual-track framework requiring both liquidity AND capital structure clarity
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS CEO's three conditions (deposit guarantee, 50bn loss buffer, regulatory indemnity) became binding constraints that shaped the entire rescue package and forced Federal Council concessions on cost exposure
marker_evidence.government_support: Federal Council's 50bn loss buffer commitment and time-limited deposit backstop were decisive concessions that enabled UBS participation — without these, UBS walks and resolution triggers
marker_evidence.client_flight: Wealth client in R2: 'if UBS walking and AT1 write-down, I'm moving assets before Monday opens' — drove the simultaneous 6 a.m. publication requirement and the Saturday drill to validate execution speed
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 write-down clause with Monday 22:00 hard trigger became the binding backstop that forced UBS to accept subordinated losses and creditors to price resolution risk — shaped the entire capital structure
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: Discussed extensively (equity vs AT1 hierarchy, who bears losses) but did not change the outcome — the Article 25 clause resolved it by making AT1 write-down the default if merger fails, no negotiation
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 rep threatened immediate litigation if write-down clause was ambiguous, forcing FINMA to add no-judicial-review language — but this was a defensive adjustment, not a decision driver
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: Monday close as hard trigger with no Tuesday negotiation window was the binding time constraint that forced all parties to lock commitments by Sunday night — drove the entire decision timeline
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Deposit velocity assumptions (20-30bn/hour if announcement has gaps) drove the simultaneous publication requirement and the 50bn facility sizing — shaped both messaging strategy and cost boundaries
